dialect: IETF network topology with layer 2 and layer 3 augmentations (RFC 8345, RFC 8944, RFC 8346)
note: Lifted semantic model, topology side. Each concept carries its lexical label, synonyms, a shallow kind, a gloss, a canonical example, the reference entry the agent bound it to (ref), plus structural relations (edges to other concept ids in this model) and concrete instances. A live side volunteers its gloss/example; an inert side exposes only label, kind, relations, and instances. ref of null marks an item with no public meaning.

concepts.label: network
concepts.gloss: one topology: the set of nodes and links that are managed together

concepts.label: node
concepts.gloss: a network device as it appears in the topology

concepts.label: termination-point
concepts.gloss: a point on a node where a link ends; with the lag flag false it is one physical port

concepts.label: lag termination-point
concepts.gloss: a termination point whose lag flag is true: several physical termination points of the same node acting as one
concepts.example: tp-9d33f163 on node-0d30dd9a, over two member termination points

concepts.label: member-link-tp
concepts.gloss: the reference from a lag termination point to each physical termination point that is one of its members
concepts.example: tp-9d33f163 has members tp-b27a3a3f and tp-b3e678d5

concepts.label: link
concepts.gloss: a connection from a source termination point on one node to a destination termination point on another node

concepts.label: rate
concepts.gloss: the bandwidth of a link, in kilobits per second

concepts.label: mac-address
concepts.gloss: the hardware address of a physical termination point

concepts.label: ip-address
concepts.gloss: an IP address held by a termination point at layer 3

concepts.label: router-id
concepts.gloss: the routing identifier of a node

concepts.label: interface-name
concepts.gloss: the name the device itself gives the interface that a termination point stands for
